We had many people in our comments who assumed we were just random people who bought a tiger cub and many people asking where they can get a tiger. We want to address this because it’s very important. Rick is not just a normal person with a tiger. Rick owns a USDA licensed zoo and Mowgli is not a personal pet. Mowgli came from another zoo and was not purchased as a pet. The reason Mowgli is inside the house (which is on the zoo property) is because he is not fully vaccinated and we will not allow him outside until our vet clears us for that. Anyone who is wanting a pet tiger needs to know that you cannot legally own one as a pet. Also, this is not Rick’s first Tiger. You can go and see Kai, our female, on our page. Rick has extensive experience with big cats and raising them. You can however enjoy how cute he is on our social media! We will NEVER have tiger encounters available and no visitors will ever be allowed to touch him or interact with him. When he is older and cleared to go outside you can see him in his enclosure if you visit the zoo. We hope that clears a few things up!

videos.caption: Grumpy Kallie is waiting for breakfast. 😊 Today, on International Tiger Day, we’re honored to introduce you to Kallie—a tiger whose survival is nothing short of a miracle. When Kallie was rescued by Lions Tigers & Bears, she had been abandoned and left to die. Her condition was so critical that she required extensive emergency medical care, multiple surgeries, and ultimately a life-saving leg amputation. Against all odds, Kallie never gave up. Today, Kallie is thriving on three legs, living the life she always deserved at Lions Tigers & Bears. She continues to receive specialized daily care from our dedicated team, and every step she takes is a reminder of what’s possible when compassion meets action. Your support made Kallie’s second chance possible. Thank you for standing with us as we rescue, rehabilitate, and provide lifelong sanctuary to animals who have nowhere else to turn. Happy International Tiger Day.

Ontario Tigers Make a Grand Entrance on Friday Night ONTARIO, Ore. - Ontario knows how to welcome its Tigers onto the field for Friday night football. As the Ontario Tigers prepared to take on the Payette Pirates, the home team made its entrance surrounded by the sights and sounds of Friday night under the lights. The Ontario band provided the rhythm, cheerleaders lined the field, and fans welcomed their team as bursts of yellow smoke filled the air. It made for an impressive entrance and a great way to begin a night of high school football between two neighboring communities. Once the game was underway, both the Tigers and Pirates had opportunities to make some great plays and give their fans something to cheer about. On this particular Friday night, however, Ontario controlled the scoreboard and earned a decisive 35–0 victory over Payette. The final score belonged to the Tigers, but Friday night football is about more than what appears on the scoreboard. It is also about the students in the band who provide the soundtrack, the cheerleaders who keep their classmates and hometown fans involved, the coaches and players representing their schools, and the families and community members filling the stands to support them. For Ontario, the evening began with quite an entrance. Red and gold, the sound of the band, cheerleaders welcoming the team and plenty of yellow smoke as the Tigers charged onto their home field. Congratulations to the Ontario Tigers on the victory, and respect to the Payette Pirates for making the trip across the river and competing through the final whistle. Two neighboring communities, two proud high school programs, and another Friday night of football in our part of the Treasure Valley. #livinginthenews #ontariohighschool #ontariotigersfootball #ontariocheer #ontarioband
